title: Fungal bioremediation of combined nickel-nanoplastic contamination in wheat:  Beauveria bassiana  restricts metal transfer and reshapes rhizosphere chemistry and metabolism
content: Nickel (Ni) contamination and polyethylene (PE) nanoplastics are emerging soil pollutants that may occur together and impose complex stresses on crop plants. However, the effects of their combined exposure and the potential role of beneficial fungi in alleviating this stress remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigated the effects of PE nanoplastics, Ni, and their combined exposure on wheat growth, physiological and biochemical responses, Ni accumulation, rhizosphere microbial communities, and plant transcriptomic and metabolomic profiles, and evaluated the potential of Beauveria bassiana Bb02 to alleviate the resulting stress. Among the seven B. bassiana strains screened, Bb02 showed the strongest growth-promoting effect and was selected for subsequent experiments. Combined Ni and PE nanoplastic exposure caused greater reductions in plant growth, photosynthetic pigments, antioxidant balance, and other physiological traits than the individual treatments. Bb02 inoculation alleviated several adverse responses, improved plant growth and physiological performance, and reduced Ni accumulation and transfer under combined contamination. Transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses further indicated that Bb02 treatment was associated with changes in stress response, antioxidant defense, hormone-related pathways, and primary and secondary metabolism. Rhizosphere microbiome analysis showed that Bb02 also altered bacterial and fungal community composition under Ni and PE nanoplastic exposure. These findings indicate that B. bassiana Bb02 can improve wheat tolerance to combined Ni and PE nanoplastic stress and is associated with changes in Ni accumulation, plant physiological responses, rhizosphere microbial communities, and molecular metabolism.
